stimulus:
The Miura-ori fold is where everyone starts, a tessellation of parallelograms that collapses along two directions at once with a single tug. Japanese space engineer Koryo Miura proposed it for solar arrays, though people love telling the story that it was inspired by subway maps, which I think is half myth. Pull one corner and the whole sheet deploys, no sequencing needed. That's the trick: one degree of freedom, a whole surface of motion.

Odd fact: Miura-ori has a negative Poisson's ratio. Stretch it one way and it expands the other way too, like a sheet that refuses to neck. Which makes me think of auxetic foams, and then of stents.

Stents! Folded paper's cousin lives in arteries. Kresling patterns, those twisted cylinders, snap between stable states like a bistable switch, a paper spring with memory. Someone built a crawling robot from them, no motors in the joints, just buckling doing the work.

Then there's rigid origami, where panels can't bend, only the creases. That matters for thick materials, because paper is conveniently thin and steel is not. Thickness ruins the math; you offset hinges, slide panels, cheat geometry.

Tangent: Robert Lang using circle packing to design a beetle's legs, which is basically optimization software wearing a kimono. Self-folding sheets with shape-memory polymer, heat-triggered, sit on a table and become a boat. DNA origami, folded strands at nanometer scale, same grammar, different dimension. Who decided a crease is a universal verb?

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Bistable switch test via hysteresis (Kresling analogy)
ideas.description: Like a Kresling cylinder snapping between stable states, test whether AP-1 activity is bistable: expose cells to graded stimulus (e.g., TPA, serum, or inducible c-Fos/c-Jun) up and then down, and measure single-cell AP-1 reporter output and target genes. Hysteresis, bimodal distributions, and persistence of the high state after stimulus removal at identical doses would indicate a self-sustaining memory state; perturbing positive feedback (c-Jun autoregulation) should abolish it.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility memory of AP-1 sites (crease persistence)
ideas.description: A fold leaves a crease that persists after the force is gone; test whether transient AP-1 activation leaves lasting accessible chromatin. Do ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors, H3K27ac and pioneer-like remodeler (BAF) occupancy at time points after stimulus washout across many cell divisions, and compare motif-defined AP-1 sites with other sites for retained accessibility and faster re-induction on restimulation.

ideas.title: Acute degron removal after priming (one-degree-of-freedom control)
ideas.description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-degradable AP-1 subunit (c-Jun/FOS/FOSL) to deplete AP-1 at defined times: during priming, during the memory interval, or only at restimulation. If memory requires AP-1 presence in the interval, depletion then erases the faster secondary response. If only priming needs it, AP-1 acts as an initiator whose crease persists without it, separating initiation from maintenance by RNA-seq and nascent transcription (PRO-seq).

ideas.title: Dynamic encoding with optogenetic pulses and live reporters
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 with optogenetic or chemically timed pulses of varying duration, frequency, and number while imaging a live AP-1 reporter and a target gene (e.g., MS2 or fluorescent knock-in). Fit models comparing response to naive versus pre-pulsed cells, to quantify memory duration, dependence on pulse history, and whether cells integrate past inputs like a mechanical system with state.

ideas.title: Lineage-resolved single-cell multiome with memory-site mutagenesis
ideas.description: Combine single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) or barcoded lineage tracing on primed versus naive cells to test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are inherited by sister cells beyond cell division. Then use CRISPR to mutate or dCas9-block specific AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers (like altering a single hinge) and test whether that selectively removes the primed response while leaving other enhancers intact.
